entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] The erosion of war and the capacity to think... Once again, American military…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

The erosion of war and the capacity to think... Once again, American military drones, missiles, and bombs have rained down on the people of the country's southern cities. Alongside material damage, a number of our compatriots have been killed. A wedding ceremony in Kohestak turned into a mourning gathering. In response, Iranian forces also targeted American bases in the Middle East with missiles. Everyone is asking: how long will these clashes continue, and where will they end? The truth is that there is no clear answer to these two questions. The American side holds contradictory positions. On one hand, they emphasize continuing pressure until the collapse of our country's security and economy, and on the other hand, they claim the goal of the pressure is to force the leaders of the Islamic Republic back to the negotiating table! On the Iranian side, despite the constant insistence by responsible officials on the need for social unity and cohesion, no single voice is heard regarding the war. While the leaders of the branches of government declare their goal to be the revival of the agreement and forcing America to implement its provisions, many other voices from within the establishment insist on opposing the agreement, continuing and expanding the war, and the necessity of resorting to preemptive operations. As such, the atmosphere on both sides of the war is ambiguous and unclear. As long as this remains the case, the war will continue intermittently along its current erosive path. The main issue, however, is: to what point can the war of attrition in its current form continue? It is clear that capacities on both sides of the war are limited, and it is impossible to sustain the current conditions even for the next few months. Therefore, it is highly likely that a dramatic event will change the current course. What will be the nature of that event, and in what direction will it shape the fate of the conflict? The nature of an "event" is its chance and accidental occurrence, and it is not predictable. Any prediction in this regard is like shooting an arrow in the dark. Even if such an arrow hits its target, it is by chance and not a sign of the predictor's knowledge and skill! In our culture, these events are called fate and destiny (qaza va qadar), and now our fate is tied to fate and destiny. All we can do is pray that the outcome is good. #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] At 61! Today I turned 61; of course, according to what's written in my ID,…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

At 61! Today I turned 61; of course, according to what's written in my ID, otherwise, according to my sisters, I was born in "Kol Kar," meaning the cotton planting season, which falls in April, from late Farvardin to mid Ordibehesht. Honestly, when I look back, I'm quite astonished at my own situation. The factors that came together to bring me from "Qaleh-ye Zardu," where I fell onto the mud floor of a dark, smoky room, to this vague present point—it's been like walking on quicksand. Was everything that happened mere coincidence? One could call it coincidence, especially in this century where not just an individual's life path but the entire universe is considered random, the result of blind forces colliding! Nevertheless, I believe every person assumes some kind of plan or destiny in the course of their life's evolution. Even those who believe in the randomness of existence are tempted, when facing grave dangers or remarkable successes, to seek an interpretation beyond pure chance in their lives. In any case, I have personally experienced something in my life with all my being: whenever, for whatever reason, my head bows from the sky toward the earth, an unpredictable and entirely unplannable event lifts my head upward. I have such faith in this experience that even if, hypothetically, all sciences and philosophies were to conclude that there's nothing up there, it would have the slightest effect on my faith in this experience! Based on my inner and outer experiences, I have accepted that not only is there something up there, but everything ends and culminates there. Hence, the most delightful and sweetest moments of my life have always been when I hold my head high. It's clear that by "up" I don't mean the geographical sense of the word. Up exists in all dimensions of being and in all directions. This too is a way of living in an era that some have perhaps wrongly or exaggeratedly called the age of the eclipse of God!#Ahmad_Zeydabadi @ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] Order to silence! The last time I told someone it would be better to stay…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

Order to silence! The last time I told someone it would be better to stay silent instead of speaking was in the middle of Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's first presidential term, addressing the late Seyed Ebrahim Nabavi. Of course, I didn't want him to be silent, but rather advised him to focus on satire and not get into serious political issues! Then I thought to myself, where does all this sense of wisdom, or really, my arrogance, come from? Why should I have the right to comment on political issues but Nabavi shouldn't? If he had turned around and told me: Why are you meddling in satirists' affairs for no reason? Sit down and write your serious stuff, how would I have felt? We have the right to criticize and reject others' opinions and ask them to be more careful, studied, and considerate in their expression, but where does the order to silence those whose views we don't like or don't find sound, for whatever reason, come from? I actually wrote this memory and its follow-up in support of the right to free speech of Mohammad Jafar Qaempanah, the vice president. Mr. Qaempanah has expressed an opinion about the importance and value of uranium enrichment in the country that some don't like, but instead of logical criticism, they call on him to be silent! Many also consider these people's own views to be wrong—would they like it if they were ordered to be silent by them? #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad

The more I scrutinize the language of the media and official authorities, the more I conclude that, in their view, the "revolutionary current" refers to none other than those who share Mr. Shariatmadari's views and the supporters of the Front of Steadfastness! Well, what is the relationship of this current with the general public? If it is merely a subset of the people and has equal rights like other citizens, then on what basis are their sensitivities and interests preferred over other segments? And if it is opposed to the rest of the people, then what is that 90-million hard core of power that is being touted? That is, according to that sarcastic poem by Vahshi Bafqi, is it to be from the courtyard to the rooftop for the "revolutionary current," and from the rooftop to the Pleiades for the rest of the people? #احمد_زیدآبادی@ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] The Path of Return Iranians abroad who see things differently from what is…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

The Path of Return
Iranians abroad who see things differently from what is commonly called the "opposition" come under psychological and media pressure. Artists, in particular, are more exposed to such pressures and negative propaganda. Eventually, a time comes when they prefer returning to their homeland, despite all its problems, over enduring those conditions, and they set their sights on going back to their birthplace. With such a decision, the political atmosphere abroad intensifies against them, and they become the target of the darkest accusations. In fact, part of the opposition seeking the overthrow of the Islamic Republic, on the one hand, treats Iranian artists abroad with utter cruelty and intolerance at the slightest divergence from their own views, and on the other hand, blocks their path back to the homeland and out of that toxic environment with endless insults! Apparently, their goal is for these artists to remain in that foreign land and die of grief! Any artist or any intellectual who does not succumb to this atmosphere and chooses the path of return to their country should be congratulated and welcomed. Living in one's homeland is the natural and God-given right of every Iranian and has nothing to do with the government. Those who deny this right or tarnish its exercise are both cut from the same cloth, standing at the two extremes of the axis of villainy! #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] It needs no one's permission, but... Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the parliament…

It needs no one's permission, but... Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the parliament speaker, has said: "The strategic relations between China and Iran need no one's permission." Yes, they need no one's permission, but do the Chinese really consider their relationship with Iran strategic? Mr. Ghalibaf has intended to travel to Beijing since his appointment as the Islamic Republic's special envoy for China affairs, but so far this trip has not materialized. Is this a coincidence? Or are the Chinese upset and angry over Iran's lack of negotiation with the US, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, threats to the energy resources of Arab Gulf states by some circles in Tehran, and especially the Houthis' actions against Saudi Arabia? China, which imports more than 40 percent of its consumed oil through the Strait of Hormuz, how could it possibly be pleased with the closure of the strait? The Saudi newspaper Arab News has reported on a high-level meeting between Chinese officials and members of the Gulf Cooperation Council in Riyadh in recent days. According to the report, "Senior officials praised the remarkable progress in implementing agreements between the parties since the announcement of the strategic partnership between the GCC and China in December 2022 and discussed initiatives to strengthen this cooperation." Doesn't this kind of news explain the direction of China's foreign policy in our region more clearly than Mr. Ghalibaf's remarks?#احمد_زیدآبادی@ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] Which massive base? The managing director of Kayhan newspaper, in his paper's…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

Which massive base? The managing director of Kayhan newspaper, in his paper's "Note" column, addressed to Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of Parliament, wrote: "Some existing evidence suggests that a Western-oriented current and a number of reformist claimants have targeted changing Mr. Ghalibaf's 'social base' and are pursuing the transfer of his social base from among the vast and devoted masses of the people to the arena of political activity of reformist claimants and Western-oriented figures." Aside from what social base Mr. Ghalibaf has, what role he now seeks to play in the country's political developments, and what capabilities and limitations he faces, it is clear that the managing director of Kayhan, in his usual manner, is throwing dust in the eyes of the Speaker of Parliament to darken his view of the stark social realities in the country. The clearest evidence for this claim is the phrase "vast and devoted masses of the people" describing the social base of the faction affiliated with the managing director of Kayhan, which, in his view, Mr. Ghalibaf is supposedly going to leave behind to shift to the "arena of political activity of reformists"! Really, which "vast mass" in this country supports the faction affiliated with Hossein Shariatmadari and counts as its social base, that he warns Mr. Ghalibaf about losing this "vast popular base"? Iranian society and its diversity are before the eyes of every one of us, and any unbiased and healthy-minded person, by taking a look around this society, can discern the true size of the base of the force favored by Mr. Shariatmadari! Given this, why does the managing director of Kayhan distort reality? Is it because, due to being disconnected from society, he does not see reality? Or does he fundamentally have no interest in seeing reality? Or is he not so unaware of reality, but sees his own interest in distorting and presenting it upside down? I usually assumed that the country's decision-makers are themselves aware of these issues and dismiss claims like those of Kayhan, but some of them apparently not only do not dismiss Kayhan's claims but have come to believe that whatever it writes is exactly reality! If this point were not at stake, I would not spend my time responding to the managing director's quibbles.
#Ahmad_Zeydabadi
@ahmadzeidabad

If it is a document of betrayal, humiliation, and surrender, it must be torn up and thrown away so that everyone's position becomes clear! entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] A bitter and failed experience! The prosecutor of Shahriar has announced the…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

A bitter and failed experience! The prosecutor of Shahriar has announced the arrest of one of the members of the Ferdowsiyeh City Council on charges of bribery! Hardly a day goes by without news like this—the arrest of a member or members of councils in various provinces of the country—being published in the media. City and village councils, which were supposed to pave the way for public participation in civic affairs and the cleansing of municipalities, have alarmingly turned into a playground for many to commit all kinds of financial corruption! Given the decline in political and social spheres, the phenomenon of city and village councils in its current form is a bitter and failed experience. Until a healthy, powerful, and free party system takes shape in the country, council elections not only fail to help improve the administration of the country's cities and villages, but, as has become evident, they add to the scope of corruption and misery. This is while the legal term of the current councils has expired more than a year ago, and the continued activity of the current councils and their elected mayors not only lacks any legal basis, but, given the worsening shortage of resources, increases the level and depth of abuse and corruption. Therefore, at least until the threat to the country is removed and the necessary stability is established, the government should prevent growing corruption in the administration of cities and villages by officially declaring the end of the legal term of the current councils and appointing new mayors by the Ministry of Interior.#Ahmad_Zeydabadi @ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] Did anyone say...? Pejman Jamshidi's sister has said; my brother is not an…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

Did anyone say...? Pejman Jamshidi's sister has said; my brother is not an Imamzadeh! Did anyone say he was an Imamzadeh? In 1996, I interviewed Mohammad Javad Larijani when he was the head of the Parliament Research Center and a disciple of Sheikh Ali Akbar Nategh Nouri, in a building in Baharestan Square. The interview was supposed to be published in Hamshahri newspaper, but the newspaper's officials found it too challenging and set it aside. In that interview, I strongly challenged Mr. Larijani on the degree of democracy in the Islamic Republic system using the criterion that Karl Popper provides, and I put him in a tight spot! He spoke a eloquent chapter in denunciation of Popper, which I answered; to hell with Popper! You tell me, according to the criterion he proposed, how democratic is the Islamic Republic? In short, to accept a low level of my criticisms, he was forced to say; the members of the Guardian Council are not infallible! I said; did anyone even entertain the suspicion of their infallibility? I should not forget to mention that the transcribed text of that interview sat in the drawer of the newspaper office's desk for a long time until Saeed Laylaz became the head of a newly established section in Hamshahri called the interview section. One night when he was left empty-handed to fill the page and was searching desperately for content, I remembered the interview with Mr. Larijani and suggested publishing it to Mr. Laylaz! Happy and smiling, he took the interview text and printed it in Hamshahri over two issues, but the challenging and valuable parts of the interview were completely removed from the published text. Regarding Pejman Jamshidi's verdict, I also did not understand the case! Apparently, the court acquitted him of the rape charge and sentenced him to flogging for an act contrary to Sharia! If there was no rape, then what other act is contrary to Sharia? Has the judge issuing the verdict not heard the recent remarks of Hassan Rahimpour Azghadi? He has explicitly said that with mutual consent, even two schoolchildren before puberty can have sexual relations and this act has no religious flaw or problem. According to Mr. Azghadi's calculation, if in the case of Mr. Jamshidi's accusation there was mutual consent, then where in the story is it contrary to Sharia that makes his flogging necessary? And if one side did not consent, then how was the acquittal of the rape charge established? #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] Honorable Peace: Seyyed Mohammad Khatami's support for an "honorable peace" has…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

Honorable Peace: Seyyed Mohammad Khatami's support for an "honorable peace" has not pleased extremist circles. Some of them ask what is meant by an "honorable peace"? Mr. Khatami himself has explained it. An honorable peace means the revival and full implementation of the memorandum officially signed between the presidents of Iran and the United States. There are three alternatives to this memorandum. First, the resumption of war, whose costs and consequences are obvious. Second, the continuation of the current situation and the persistence of the economic siege of the country, whose consequences need no explanation. Third, accepting a unilateral formula that does not lead to the lifting of sanctions. Which of these three alternatives is sweet to the extremists that they deny the implementation of the memorandum as the basis of an honorable peace? #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] Defective Structure of Consciousness! Why is there so much emphasis in Persian…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

Defective Structure of Consciousness! Why is there so much emphasis in Persian literature on learning lessons from history? For the obvious reason that we Iranians have the least interest in learning lessons from history; otherwise, why would this topic be repeated to such an extent? The experience of August 28, 1953 (28 Mordad 1332) is right before our eyes! No political force can be found that has learned the necessary lesson from that event. The descendants of all the forces that played a role, negatively or positively, in that catastrophe are not only repeating those mistakes but have intensified their errors. Is it, as Ahmad Shamlou said, that our historical memory as Iranians is weak? The weakness of historical memory is not without a role in this matter, but in my opinion, the "defective structure of consciousness" plays a much larger role. The structure of consciousness in any society, in my view, is much more important than other structures, and until it is reformed, the reform of political and social structures seems impossible. Political and social structures can be shattered by revolt and revolution, but if the structure of consciousness is not sound, those two structures will be reproduced in a more horrific way. Reforming the structure of consciousness of a society, however, is infinitely difficult, because first, reaching a collective agreement on the criteria for whether a thought or consciousness is defective or sound, especially in a society where everyone is infatuated with their own thoughts, is beyond difficulty. Second, the prerequisite for reforming the structure of society's consciousness begins with self-criticism and continues with the necessary patience to convince others through discussion and dialogue. In our country, self-criticism is considered a sign of weakness and is truly seen as self-flagellation. Hence, finding faults must be sought not in one's own camp but in the opposing camp. When we do not acknowledge any weakness for ourselves and see our own camp at the "tip of the arrow of historical evolution!" it is natural that we also do not find the patience for persuasive dialogue and consider the elimination, disregard, and belittlement of others as an easier path! In short, for historical reasons, we have developed a defective structure of consciousness, and again for historical reasons, we have shown and do not show any interest in reforming it. Hence, we repeat our fate in a closed circle. This time, however, the previously traveled paths are also blocked. Therefore, the most astonishing events in history await us. #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad
